ENGLISH — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

2. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. run
   C. blue
   D. happiness

3. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goes
   C. going
   D. goed

4. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library

5. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

6. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

7. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

8. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

9. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a describing word

10. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

12. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

13. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.

14. When practising Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.

15. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Narrative Composition 14.5.1 Descriptive writing 15.5.1 Functional Writing –Noti and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 14.4.1 Features of style and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Descriptive writing 15.5.1 Functional Writing –Notices and Posters and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
